newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader arrives in triumph in Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader arrives in triumph in Kisangani.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila arrived in the capital of northeastern Zaire on Friday, rejecting a truce and hailed as a saviour by more than 10,000 jubilant residents.
Asked by reporters at Kisangani airport whether he could accept a ceasefire call by ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, Kabila told reporters: "We negotiate first."
The rebel leader says he wants negotiations with Mobutu, or his representative, before any ceasefire and he will only talk about how the 66-year-old ruler plans to step down from power.
It was Kabila's first visit to Kisangani since it fell to rebel forces last Saturday. He flew in from the eastern city of Goma, which fell to rebels early in the revolt which began last October.
Crowds sang hymns as Kabila arrived. One fervent supporter carried a placard proclaiming: "It is God who has sent Kabila to come down and be amongst us."
"We are waiting for Kabila. He is our Moses," said Alpha Kangudi, a 23-year-old student.
Kabila, wearing a stetson hat, looked cheerful.
Bodyguards worked to clear thousands of euphoric people crammed into the airport and wearing white bandanas symbolic of support for the rebel cause.
Two planes landed at the airport before Kabila's. The first, carrying his armed escort, was mobbed by the crowd.
Hundreds of people lined the route into the city on the Zaire River waving palm branches and singing. Kabila was whisked away to rebel headquarters at a hotel to meet city officials.
Shortly before Kabila landed in Kisangani, rebel political commissioner Deo Bugera also rejected a truce.
Asked about Mobutu's ceasefire call and return to Kinshasa from France, Bugera said: "We do not receive Mobutu's orders. If Mobutu comes back it makes no difference.
"We are going to liberate our people. He always wants to buy time. But we will not play his game."
Diplomats said United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun was expected in Kisangani later on Friday after talks with Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni to press Kabila for a truce.
Mobutu left France on Friday to return to Kinshasa.

The rebels have seized more than a fifth of Zaire since launching their revolt in the east and Kabila says his forces will press on to the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi and Zaire's second city Lubumbashi.
